title: Hiring manager, mid designer, average answers, coach mode

questions.text: Walk me through a design project you are proud of and your role in it.
Tell me about a time you disagreed with a stakeholder about a design direction.
What draws you to this team?
How do you decide what to design next when many requests compete?
How do you work with engineers during build?
How do you handle critique of your work?

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Hi Camille, thanks for joining. I'm Daniel, design manager for the mobile team. We have thirty minutes to talk about your work and how you think.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Hi Daniel, nice to meet you. Thank you for having me.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How is your week going so far?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Pretty good. I just finished a round of user tests, so I'm tired but happy.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: This is a practice session, so I may add a short tip at the end. I'll ask about a few projects, and then you can ask me things.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Walk me through a design project you are proud of and your role in it.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I'm proud of the onboarding flow redesign for a budgeting app at Quillon Labs. We saw many people dropping off after sign up. I did the research with five users, then sketched new screens and tested them. We shortened the flow from seven steps to four, and sign up completion went up, I think by around 15 percent. Engineering built it over about a month.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What was your part compared to the rest of the team?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I did the flows, the screens and the prototype. The product manager set the goal and one researcher helped me with the interviews, but I wrote the test plan. I also made the handoff files for the engineers.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How did you know the four step version was the right one?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I ran a test with six users on both versions. Five of six finished the four step flow without help, and only two finished the old one. I did not test other lengths, so I am not sure four is the best number.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a stakeholder about a design direction.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: A product manager wanted a banner on the home screen for a new feature. I thought it would push down the main content. We talked a few times and I showed mockups of both. In the end we added a smaller card instead. It worked out.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How did the card perform?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I think people clicked it enough, because the manager did not bring it up again. Later I asked analytics, and about 8 percent of users tapped the card. That was lower than the banner estimate, but it kept the main content visible. I would make the same trade again.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How do you decide what to design next when many requests compete?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I usually ask the product manager what matters most. Then I look at which request affects the most users. I make a short list and share it with the team so everyone can see it. If two things conflict I ask for a decision.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Can you give me a real case?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Last quarter I had requests for a settings page, a new chart and a list of bug fixes. I ranked them by users affected and effort. The bug fixes went first because they touched about 60 percent of users.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Thanks. What questions do you have for me?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: How closely do designers work with engineers on your team?

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Each designer is paired with two engineers and sits in their standup. Designers also review the built screens before release.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: That is all the time we have. A tip from the practice session is to lead with the number in each story. Thanks Camille.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: That is helpful, thank you Daniel.

notes: Average for mid: some numbers but hedged, and one generic answer that the interviewer probes.
